title: Adentris vs Sohar Health: Eligibility vs Documentation Compliance Compared
summary: Adentris vs Sohar Health for behavioral health and SUD: automated eligibility and benefits verification versus documentation compliance that prevents denials, with ASAM, 42 CFR Part 2, and appeals.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** Sohar Health and Adentris both protect behavioral health revenue, but at different points in the workflow. Sohar automates insurance eligibility verification and verification of benefits before care, so coverage is confirmed up front. Adentris reviews the documentation before the claim is submitted, catching the gaps that drive denials, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module built in. If your leak is eligibility and benefits at intake, Sohar is built for that. If your leak is documentation and denials after the visit, that is where Adentris focuses. They are complementary.


Both protect behavioral health revenue, but at opposite ends of the visit, so the comparison is about which leak you are closing. Here is the honest breakdown.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What Sohar Health does


Sohar Health is an API-first AI platform that automates insurance eligibility verification and verification of benefits for behavioral health providers, confirming coverage quickly at intake with a fast median response time. By catching coverage and benefit problems before care is delivered, it helps prevent eligibility-related denials. For behavioral health providers who want to automate front-end insurance checks, Sohar is a strong, focused option.

## Which should you choose?


Sohar works at the front of the visit: confirming that the patient is covered and what the benefits are before care is delivered, which prevents eligibility-related denials. Adentris works at the back of the visit: making sure the documentation supports the claim before it is submitted, which prevents documentation-related denials. It flags a missing medical necessity statement, an unjustified ASAM level of care, or a missing 42 CFR Part 2 consent, drafts the correction, and pairs review with an appeals and denials module. Because they close different leaks, many behavioral health programs use both.


- **Choose Sohar Health if** you want to automate front-end insurance eligibility and benefit checks so coverage is confirmed before care.
- **Choose Adentris if** your denials come from documentation rather than coverage, and you want the note checked against payer and regulatory criteria before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth and an appeals workflow, on any EHR.


## Adentris as a complement to Sohar Health for documentation denials


Sohar Health and Adentris are complementary rather than alternatives. Sohar prevents eligibility-related denials at intake; Adentris prevents documentation-related denials before the claim goes out. If you have automated eligibility but still lose claims after care, the gap is usually documentation: a missing medical necessity statement, an unjustified ASAM level of care, or a 42 CFR Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris is built around exactly those gaps, drafts the fix before submission, pairs it with an appeals and denials workflow, and runs on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, so it slots in alongside a front-end eligibility tool.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. In practice that means fewer denied claims, less audit exposure, and far less time spent reworking documentation after a payer pushes back. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. ## The bottom line


Sohar Health protects revenue at intake by confirming coverage; Adentris protects it after the visit by making sure the documentation gets paid. They close different leaks, so many behavioral health programs run both.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and Sohar Health?**


Sohar Health automates insurance eligibility verification and verification of benefits for behavioral health providers before care. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note before the claim is submitted, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals module. Sohar prevents eligibility-related denials up front; Adentris prevents documentation-related denials after the visit.


**Can Adentris and Sohar Health be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use Sohar Health to verify eligibility and benefits and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside Sohar Health.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to Sohar Health?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than front-end eligibility and benefits, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. Sohar Health is strong for automating insurance eligibility and verification of benefits. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
